worst_three_phrases.english: but I make to me today
worst_three_phrases.reason: This is a fragment from 'ich mache mir Sorgen' (I worry) that has been incorrectly isolated. The English is a literal word-for-word translation that makes no sense. The German is incomplete - it needs an object. This should never appear as a standalone phrase.

worst_three_phrases.english: it is too much to take time to answer
worst_three_phrases.other: es ist zu viel Zeit zum Antworten brauchen
worst_three_phrases.reason: The English is grammatically awkward with unclear meaning. The German has 'brauchen' (to need) tacked on incorrectly - the structure mixes two different constructions. Should be either 'es braucht zu viel Zeit zum Antworten' or 'es dauert zu lange zu antworten'.

worst_three_phrases.english: I do not like too much time to learn German with you
worst_three_phrases.other: ich mag nicht zu viel Zeit Deutsch mit dir zu lernen
worst_three_phrases.reason: Both languages have broken syntax. The intended meaning is unclear - possibly 'I don't like spending too much time learning German with you' but the current phrasing doesn't express this. The German structure with 'moegen' + time expression + infinitive clause doesn't work.

quality_assessment.strong_7_8: 46% - Majority are strong with minor issues
quality_assessment.overall: Good quality overall (7.38 avg). The problematic phrases (12%) appear to be LEGO fragment isolation issues or complex constructions that broke during generation. The 'starting well' test shows 88% of phrases are functional or better.

common_issues: Fragment isolation: Phrases like 'but I make to me today' are incomplete idiom fragments
Complex constructions: Double infinitives and nested clauses sometimes have word order errors
Umlaut encoding: Some phrases show 'mude' instead of 'muede' - minor transcription issue
'indifferent to' translation: English uses slightly unusual phrasing for 'egal' (better: 'I don't care')
recommendations: Review LEGO decomposition for 'sich Sorgen machen' - fragments should not stand alone
Check double infinitive constructions for correct verb-final order
Verify 'egal' translations use natural English equivalents
